facts.label: Bottom line

Megger pro forma is incomplete; High; Megger EBITDA, debt, cash, fees, financing costs and the closing day are not supplied; the pro forma uses the approximate cash portion of about USD 0.9 billion on ESCO standalone EBITDA; The pro forma net leverage of 2.98x is a mechanical figure that omits Megger earnings and debt; Add Megger financial statements and the acquisition and financing agreements

Adjusted EBITDA is not stated for fiscal years; Medium; Adjusted EBITDA is stated for the three, six and nine month periods and quarters of fiscal 2026 and 2025 but not for fiscal 2023, 2024 or 2025; Adjusted total debt to EBITDA, net debt to adjusted EBITDA and adjusted cover are not calculable at any of the five dates; Obtain fiscal year adjusted EBITDA from the fourth quarter release

Debt stack and legal rank not stated; Medium; No source states the legal rank of the revolver relative to the term loan A, and the security of the term loan A is not stated separately; The debt stack chart is not drawn and senior secured debt cannot be separated; Obtain the executed credit agreement and amendment

EBITDA bridge not stated item by item; Medium; The issuer states adjustments per share after tax and by segment, not as pretax add-backs by item, so no bridge from reported to adjusted EBITDA reconciles without a plug; The bridge chart states no amounts; Obtain pretax adjustment amounts

Current portion of debt described two ways; Medium; The USD 20 million current portion has no contractual repayment obligation in the annual report and the December 2025 report but is obligated by the incremental facility repayment terms in the March and June 2026 reports; The maturity ladder shows USD 20 million due within twelve months on the later wording; Obtain the repayment schedule in the executed agreement

Covenant levels not printed; Medium; The notes name a leverage ratio and an interest coverage ratio and state compliance at each date, but no level, step-down or definition; Covenant headroom is not calculable and is not inferred; Obtain the executed credit agreement

Fiscal 2023 balance sheet; Low; The balance sheet at 2023-09-30 is not in the sources; No debt, cash or leverage for fiscal 2023; Obtain the fiscal 2024 annual report

Printed dashes and interim line coverage; Low; Lines printed as a dash are written as not supplied and not read as zero; interim statements omit the annual gain on sale line, the treasury purchase and debt issuance cost lines (except the nine month debt issuance cost) and the working capital components; Several cells in the statement tables state a gap; None: the sources print no further detail

Lease liabilities outside debt; Medium; Operating lease liabilities of 50.260 and finance lease liabilities of 15.396 at 2026-06-30 sit on other balance sheet lines and are not in Total Debt; Lease-adjusted leverage is not calculated; State a lease-adjusted measure if the credit view requires it

Maritime not in the earlier twelve-month sums; Medium; Twelve-month EBITDA at 2025-12-31 and 2026-03-31, and fiscal 2025, include Maritime only from 2025-04-25 and are not pro forma; Leverage at those dates is overstated relative to a full year of Maritime; the trend from 2025-09-30 mixes repayment and acquired earnings; Add pro forma Maritime EBITDA if a source states it

No discrete fourth quarter of fiscal 2025; Low; The fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 is not printed; it is the annual figure less the nine month figure; Discrete fourth quarter trends are not shown; None needed for the twelve-month sums

facts.text: No controlling shareholder or sponsor is evidenced, so there is no owner whose support or extraction can be assessed, and creditor protection rests on the bank documents and public reporting. ESCO is a Missouri corporation listed on the New York Stock Exchange; the sources name no controlling holder, and directors, officers and holders of five percent or more appear only in a proxy statement that is not supplied. The articles also provide a classified board and a two-thirds vote for mergers under Missouri law, which make a change of control harder. The absence of a named sponsor removes dividend recapitalization and sponsor fees as documented risks, but the control position stays unproven until the proxy statement is read. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: ESCO spends cash on acquisitions rather than on shareholders, which protects creditors until the next deal changes the balance sheet. Cash paid for acquisitions over fiscal 2023 to 2025 was USD 546.08 million against USD 45.16 million of dividends and share purchases, or 12.09x. The dividend has stayed at USD 0.32 per share a year, no shares were bought in fiscal 2025 or in the first nine months of fiscal 2026, and the VACCO sale for about USD 270 million was used primarily to pay down debt. Goodwill and intangible assets are 58.87% of total assets, so asset value rests on the earnings of acquired businesses, and a buyback authority of up to USD 200 million to 2027-09-30 remains unused. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The view would turn adverse if closing gave TBG AG a large holding with board, consent or sale rights, if the new term loans were drawn in full without Megger earnings to match, if the credit agreements allowed distributions or buybacks that conduct has not yet used, or if the proxy statement named a large holder with interests apart from creditors. It would turn more favorable if the Shareholder Agreement limited TBG AG's rights and transfers, Megger's earnings and debt proved modest against the price, and the covenant levels left wide headroom. A termination of the Megger agreement would return the analysis to the stable position before the deal. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The Megger acquisition is the dominant credit event and cannot yet be sized. Net debt to EBITDA would rise from 0.04x to 2.98x pro forma for the cash price, with closing expected in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, and that figure uses ESCO's own EBITDA only, with no Megger earnings and no Megger debt. The total price of about USD 2.35 billion is 7.69x ESCO's last-twelve-months EBITDA and 97.11% of its total assets, the cash part alone is 2.94x, and the equity part, 59.57% of the price, adds no debt but adds a shareholder. As an illustration, interest on USD 0.9 billion at the existing facility's recent average rate of 5.18% would be about USD 46.62 million a year, 15.25% of last-twelve-months EBITDA, but the new facility's pricing is not supplied. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Margins are stable to rising and cost flexibility is moderate. EBITDA margin was 23.68% over the last twelve months against 22.40% in fiscal 2025 and 21.58% in fiscal 2024, A&D earned a segment margin of 28.41% in the nine months, the company attributes higher segment margins to volume leverage and price increases partly offset by inflationary pressures, and capital expenditure is only 3.32% of sales. facts.label: Competitive forces, external factors and opportunities and threats
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is broad and global, with named competitors in each segment including Parker Hannifin, Moog and TransDigm in aerospace, Megger and OMICRON in utility testing and Rohde & Schwarz in shielding, and competition is driven by quality, technology, price and delivery, so no single factor protects margin. The company points to patented technology and Doble's reserve of empirical data as barriers to new entrants (Management Language), which would support margin durability if they hold. Substitution is not described as a risk for qualified aerospace and naval products, and the pressure at NRG comes from renewables policy rather than from substitutes. Buyer power is meaningful: government contracts can be terminated for the customer's convenience and appropriations can delay orders, though no customer exceeds 10% of sales. Supplier power is concentrated in sole-source parts, such as the single manufacturer behind about 23% of Doble products and Globe's single supplier of critical materials. citations.quote: Competitive rivalry is broad and global, with named competitors in each segment including Parker Hannifin, Moog and TransDigm in aerospace, Megger and OMICRON in utility testing and Rohde & Schwarz in shielding, and competition is driven by quality, technology, price and delivery, so no single factor protects margin. The company points to patented technology and Doble's reserve of empirical data as barriers to new entrants (Management Language), which would support margin durability if they hold. Substitution is not described as a risk for qualified aerospace and naval products, and the pressure at NRG comes from renewables policy rather than from substitutes. Buyer power is meaningful: government contracts can be terminated for the customer's convenience and appropriations can delay orders, though no customer exceeds 10% of sales. Supplier power is concentrated in sole-source parts, such as the single manufacturer behind about 23% of Doble products and Globe's single supplier of critical materials.

facts.label: Competitive forces, external factors and opportunities and threats
facts.text: Macro and policy factors are material to credit here, so the external-factor review is kept. Political and regulatory: defense spending priorities, export controls and tariffs, UK naval funding and trade tension with China can delay orders or raise costs, and Asia is a tenth of sales. Economic: inflation squeezes fixed-price margins, and interest rates apply to the floating-rate bank debt. Technological and end-market: broad-based utility demand and data-center filters lifted Doble and Test orders, while the expiry of U.S. renewables tax credits cut NRG orders. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: A realistic downside starts with a delay or cut in U.S. Government funding for Navy submarine programs, which Globe and Westland depend on and which the company says can extend beyond a single year, arriving while Megger has closed and the new term loans are drawn. The first operational break is in A&D, the largest segment at 49.29% of nine-month sales: program deliveries slip, backlog converts later, and customer advances stop growing, so the USD 71.55 million build in contract liabilities starts to reverse. EBITDA and operating cash flow fall together, free cash flow conversion drops back toward the 60.41% of fiscal 2025, and on today's liquidity of USD 515.54 million, 7.21x the contract liability build, the reversal alone would be absorbed, although liquidity after closing depends on the new revolver and the cash used for the price, which are not established. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The financial consequence depends on the Megger debt. On ESCO's own EBITDA, net debt to EBITDA would already stand at 2.98x after the cash price, and any EBITDA fall raises it mechanically, but the size of the fall that would breach a covenant cannot be computed because covenant levels, the new facility's pricing and Megger's earnings are not supplied. Standalone, interest cover would stay at 10.21x even if EBITDA halved, and management levers are the dividend of USD 8.26 million, the unused buyback authority, capital expenditure of only 3.32% of sales and the equity portion of the Megger price. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress on the standalone business; after closing it cannot be confirmed, and the observable triggers are the closing notice, the drawn amounts under the new term loans, the first covenant disclosure and the next quarter's backlog and orders. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, ESCO presents a strong standalone business profile supported by net debt of USD 11.76 million, cash interest cover of 20.42x, liquidity of USD 515.54 million and backlog of USD 1,540.5 million, but credit quality is constrained by the pending Megger acquisition, which would lift net debt to USD 911.76 million pro forma and add a shareholder whose rights are unknown. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because conversion is 84.44% of EBITDA over the last twelve months against 60.41% in fiscal 2025, part of the gap is customer-advance timing, and part of the demand rests on government funding. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the Megger closing and the terms of the new facility, since the existing facility matures on 2028-08-30 and no rating or market data are supplied. The primary downside path is a government funding delay at A&D arriving after Megger closes with debt-funded cash. Further analysis would require Megger's financial statements, the credit agreements and the Shareholder Agreement. The module is ready with limitations, because the source gate is partly met: the seven public documents and the three earlier analyses are present, but the credit agreements and Megger's financials are not. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: the leverage step-up from the Megger acquisition. spans.text: # CP-1 Financial foundation for ESCO TECHNOLOGIES INC (ese)
## Request

Financial foundation for ESCO TECHNOLOGIES INC (ese), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and interest cover from the seven supplied filings and releases, in USD, with fiscal years ending September 30.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025, audited | 2025-12-01 | fe80d5d10f35aaa7f1b7aa40e6d69aeaea7f501fabdde619947c03aa0fe69d71 | Fiscal 2023 to 2025 statements, debt and lease notes, segment note, EBIT and D&A |

| 10-Q_2025-12-31_ese-20251231x10q.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-09 | 028e0b9aec25ecf720ca796f0beef13fd8b40ddc333348a8ba8153fe3b16e523 | Three-month statements, debt and liquidity text |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_ese-20260331x10q.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-05-11 | d207365eeea17e17e69c10625b481ddba582ee4861f7a9c60376e4bd5dffc806 | Six-month statements, debt and liquidity text |

| EX-99.1_2026-05-07_tm2613615d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) for the fiscal second quarter 2026 | 2026-05-07 | 4483c93985a6b3ea98a959d8659fafa040f3230850186662a7c5bb7c5d2d8a1d | Stated EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA, segment sales |

| EX-99.1_2026-08-06_tm2621646d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) for the fiscal third quarter 2026 | 2026-08-06 | f683102e1a6a6e74cee756fd0639a64a1d810e0d5fd17fcb2dc502f25f716fb6 | Stated EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA, guidance, backlog, dividend date |

| Source readiness handoff (CP-0) | Source readiness for this run, module CP-0 | not stated | fbe193dfee5c7348fcd056e3b5fb7934b942cd2c9bbedbc8d3b10784806a39da | Source set, gaps and the definition conflicts it records |
## Findings
### Bottom line

ESCO carries very little leverage on reported figures: net debt was USD 11.76 million, or 0.04x last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 305.68 million at 2026-06-30, so existing creditors are well covered until the pending Megger acquisition closes. Pro forma for Megger's cash consideration of about USD 0.9 billion, net debt would be about USD 911.76 million, or 2.98x ESCO's own EBITDA; the closing date is not stated beyond the first quarter of fiscal 2027.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C13; calculation C20; calculation C71

Cash interest cover was 20.42x and undrawn revolver capacity was USD 442.3 million against total debt of USD 85 million, with USD 20 million classified as due within twelve months and the rest due by 2028-08-30. The company states adjusted EBITDA only for interim periods, so leverage here is on reported EBITDA, and nothing after the June 2026 quarter is supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_tm2621646d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C52; calculation C36; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

Reported leverage has fallen because debt was repaid while earnings grew. Total debt fell from USD 186 million at 2025-09-30 to USD 85 million at 2026-06-30, and last-twelve-months EBITDA rose from USD 245.38 million to USD 305.68 million, which took total debt to EBITDA from 0.76x to 0.28x and net debt to EBITDA from 0.34x to 0.04x. The repayment came from operating cash flow of USD 193.38 million from continuing operations in the nine months to 2026-06-30 and from a USD 28.11 million fall in cash, and the Maritime acquisition, owned since 2025-04-25, lifted the earnings base.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C20; calculation C50; calculation C51

Interest cover is strong and improving. Last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 305.68 million against cash interest paid of USD 14.97 million gives 20.42x, up from 14.09x in fiscal 2025, because debt fell and the weighted average rate on the revolver eased to 4.98% in the quarter to 2026-06-30. Cash interest paid, not the interest expense line, is the denominator, since the June 2026 quarter's expense includes about USD 7 million of financing costs for the pending acquisition.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 23; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_tm2621646d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C52; calculation C21

Cash flow quality is good but flattered by customer advances. Operating cash flow from continuing operations was USD 193.38 million in the nine months to 2026-06-30 against USD 88.30 million a year earlier, and free cash flow after capital expenditure and capitalized software was USD 160.94 million. Including discontinued operations the figure is USD 134.04 million, because discontinued operations used USD 59.34 million, which the company ties to about USD 59 million of cash taxes on the VACCO gain paid in the second quarter.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C32

Contract liabilities, customer advances that fund working capital, rose from USD 80.84 million at 2024-09-30 to USD 216.59 million at 2025-09-30, mainly through the Maritime acquisition and growth at Globe and Doble, and to USD 288.14 million at 2026-06-30, which the company attributes to the timing of customer payments at Globe and Maritime. That float supports cash generation and would unwind if deliveries outpace new advances, so part of the strong cash flow is timing, not earnings.

Liquidity is ample against the debt. At 2026-06-30 cash was USD 73.24 million and the undrawn part of the USD 500 million revolver was USD 442.3 million after USD 45 million of borrowings and USD 12.7 million of letters of credit. The revolver and the incremental term loan both mature on 2028-08-30, so no facility expires within twelve months, although USD 20 million of term loan principal is classified as current.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; calculation C36

The strongest contrary evidence is the pending Megger acquisition, so these figures describe the company before closing. About USD 0.9 billion of the USD 2.35 billion price is cash; if paid from cash or new debt, net debt would be about USD 911.76 million, or 2.98x ESCO's own EBITDA before any Megger earnings, and new bank facilities of USD 500 million each for a revolver, a term loan A and a term loan B replace the existing facility on closing. Megger's own EBITDA, debt and cash are not supplied, so a closing inside the first quarter of fiscal 2027 with offsetting earnings would change the reading; so would any news that the deal did not close.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_tm2621646d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C71

Three definition points limit comparisons. Annual EBITDA is calculated as EBIT plus depreciation and amortization on the issuer's own construction because the company states EBITDA only for interim periods; debt excludes USD 50.26 million of operating and USD 15.40 million of finance lease liabilities that sit on other balance sheet lines; and the USD 20 million current portion is described as having no contractual repayment obligation in the annual report and the December 2025 report but as obligated in the March and June 2026 reports.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-Q_2025-12-31_ese-20251231x10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-03-31_ese-20260331x10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 17; Source readiness (CP-0)

The VACCO sale shows how one event carries several figures with different roles: net proceeds of about USD 270 million, an investing inflow of USD 268.38 million in discontinued operations, an after-tax gain of USD 172.64 million, and about USD 59 million of cash taxes paid in the second quarter of fiscal 2026. Each is carried on its own line and none is netted against another.

Events after the balance sheet date are kept out of period figures: a dividend of USD 0.08 per share paid on 2026-07-17, a further dividend of the same amount payable on 2026-10-15, and the Megger closing expected in the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The table of post-balance-sheet adjustments states each effect on net debt and leverage.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 25; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_tm2621646d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C72

spans.text: # CP-1A Business & governance for ESCO TECHNOLOGIES INC (ese)
## Request

Business & governance for ESCO TECHNOLOGIES INC (ese), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business, ownership, transactions, operating model, governance and owner or sponsor behavior that the seven supplied documents state, read from a creditor's position.
## Sources

| EX-99.1_2026-05-07_tm2613615d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) for the fiscal second quarter 2026 | 2026-05-07 | 4483c93985a6b3ea98a959d8659fafa040f3230850186662a7c5bb7c5d2d8a1d | Megger status and expected closing, guidance |

| Source readiness handoff (CP-0) | Source readiness for this run, module CP-0 | not stated | fbe193dfee5c7348fcd056e3b5fb7934b942cd2c9bbedbc8d3b10784806a39da | Source set, content map, document dates and definition conflicts |
## Findings
### Bottom line

ESCO, a listed aerospace, utility-testing and RF-testing group, has no sponsor or controlling shareholder named in the sources, so creditors rely on bank documents and disclosure, and the pending Megger acquisition will test that by adding secured bank debt and a new shareholder.

Megger, a testing supplier to electric utilities, is priced at about USD 2.35 billion, which is 97.11% of ESCO's total assets at 2026-06-30, paid with USD 0.9 billion of cash and about USD 1.4 billion of ESCO shares to the seller, TBG AG, whose holding and rights the sources do not state. Closing was expected in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and no document after 2026-08-10 is supplied, so ownership and debt at the 2026-11-05 cutoff are not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_tm2621646d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C55; calculation C62; calculation C63; calculation C64; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

No controlling shareholder or sponsor is evidenced, so there is no owner whose support or extraction can be assessed, and creditor protection rests on the bank documents and public reporting. ESCO is a Missouri corporation listed on the New York Stock Exchange; the sources name no controlling holder, and directors, officers and holders of five percent or more appear only in a proxy statement that is not supplied. The articles also provide a classified board and a two-thirds vote for mergers under Missouri law, which make a change of control harder. The absence of a named sponsor removes dividend recapitalization and sponsor fees as documented risks, but the control position stays unproven until the proxy statement is read.

The Megger purchase is the credit event: it is large against the balance sheet and changes both the debt and the shareholder base. The agreed price is about USD 2.35 billion, 97.11% of total assets and 1.45x shareholders' equity at 2026-06-30, and 4.98x the cash price paid for Maritime, the largest earlier deal. About USD 0.9 billion is cash, funded from existing cash and incremental debt with committed financing, and about USD 1.4 billion is ESCO equity. The stated cash and equity parts add to USD 50 million less than the stated total, which the filings repeat without reconciling.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_ese-20260331x10q.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 59; calculation C55; calculation C56; calculation C58; calculation C61; calculation C63; calculation C64

The new bank facilities exceed the stated cash price, but most of their terms are unstated. The credit agreement signed on 2026-05-29 provides a USD 500 million senior secured revolver, a USD 500 million senior secured term loan A and a USD 500 million senior secured term loan B, commitments of USD 1.5 billion against USD 85 million drawn today, and the term loans alone exceed the cash portion by USD 100 million. It becomes effective on conditions that include the Megger closing, and it replaces the existing facility then. Pricing, amortization, guarantors, collateral scope and covenants are not supplied, so the new lenders' protection and the covenant headroom cannot be assessed.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C65; calculation C67; calculation C68

The seller will become a shareholder whose influence cannot yet be judged. A Shareholder Agreement with TBG AG is to be signed at completion and appears only in the exhibit list, and no share count, issue price, board right, transfer restriction or voting term is supplied. TBG AG's percentage holding and its power over dividends, share issuance or a later sale are therefore not established, and this is a question of capacity: no willingness of TBG AG is inferred from its identity.

ESCO spends cash on acquisitions rather than on shareholders, which protects creditors until the next deal changes the balance sheet. Cash paid for acquisitions over fiscal 2023 to 2025 was USD 546.08 million against USD 45.16 million of dividends and share purchases, or 12.09x. The dividend has stayed at USD 0.32 per share a year, no shares were bought in fiscal 2025 or in the first nine months of fiscal 2026, and the VACCO sale for about USD 270 million was used primarily to pay down debt. Goodwill and intangible assets are 58.87% of total assets, so asset value rests on the earnings of acquired businesses, and a buyback authority of up to USD 200 million to 2027-09-30 remains unused.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C48; calculation C51; calculation C52; calculation C54

The business is moving toward Navy and aerospace work under government contracts, which gives visibility but concentrates demand on defense budgets. The A&D segment rose from 34.14% of net sales in fiscal 2023 to 49.29% in the nine months to 2026-06-30 after the Maritime purchase, at a segment margin of 28.41% against 26.17% in fiscal 2025. Government customers were 31.63% of fiscal 2025 sales against 23.32% a year earlier, government contracts can be terminated for the customer's convenience, and backlog reached USD 1,540.5 million at 2026-06-30, of which about 59% is expected to convert within twelve months.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 88; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C01; calculation C10; calculation C22; calculation C19; calculation C25; calculation C26

Reporting is timely and audited, but governance detail and lender terms are missing. The auditor, Grant Thornton, gave unqualified opinions on the fiscal 2025 statements and on internal control, and management excluded Maritime from its internal control assessment, covering 24.3% of consolidated assets and 8.7% of net sales. Two directors are officers of two Doble customers with sales of about USD 4.7 million, which is 0.43% of net sales, and the board judged this not material. Board composition, committee roles, five percent holders and the covenant levels are not supplied.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 89; calculation C45

Concentration pockets in operations could slow deliveries or growth. One supplier produces about 23% of Doble's products from a single location, and NRG sales fell 29% in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 as renewables demand weakened, which offsets part of the growth at Doble. Capital needs are light, with capital expenditures of 3.32% of net sales in fiscal 2025.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 23; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_tm2621646d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 59; calculation C46
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a governance concern is ESCO's conduct so far: it has no sponsor, pays a flat dividend of USD 0.32 per share a year, has bought no shares since fiscal 2024, used the VACCO proceeds primarily to pay down debt, and arranged the Maritime financing through a lender-approved amendment. Before Megger its funded debt was only USD 85 million, so the new debt starts from a low base and no creditor-adverse action is documented.

The view would turn adverse if closing gave TBG AG a large holding with board, consent or sale rights, if the new term loans were drawn in full without Megger earnings to match, if the credit agreements allowed distributions or buybacks that conduct has not yet used, or if the proxy statement named a large holder with interests apart from creditors. It would turn more favorable if the Shareholder Agreement limited TBG AG's rights and transfers, Megger's earnings and debt proved modest against the price, and the covenant levels left wide headroom. A termination of the Megger agreement would return the analysis to the stable position before the deal.
### Limitations

- The sources end with filings dated 2026-08-10, so whether Megger closed, who then holds ESCO shares and which facility is in force at the 2026-11-05 cutoff are not established, and a closing would turn the ownership and transaction findings from pending to actual.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_tm2621646d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 3; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Megger's revenue, earnings, debt and cash, and the number and issue price of the ESCO shares, are not supplied, so the size of TBG AG's holding and the mix of the enlarged utility segment cannot be computed, and either could change the view of dilution and of segment concentration.

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so board composition, five percent holders and insider holdings are not established, and the finding that no controlling holder exists would change if a large holder were named.

- The credit agreements are not supplied, so legal capacity for dividends, buybacks, investments and liens is not established, and the finding that shareholder returns are restrained rests on behavior, not on what the documents permit.

- The business description dates from the annual report of 2025-12-01 and later documents update only sales, profit, backlog and transactions, so customer concentration beyond the 10% threshold and seasonality are not established and the revenue durability reading rests on backlog and segment data.
### Company and operating model
| Operating measure | FY2025 | FY2024 | Change | Creditor consequence | Source |

| Net sales, continuing operations | USD 1,095.388 million | USD 919.127 million | USD 176.261 million, 19.18% | Growth is partly bought: Maritime added USD 95.2 million of FY2025 sales, so earnings scale rests on acquired businesses as well as organic demand | 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 74 |

| A&D share of net sales | 43.66% | 37.05% | 6.61 pp | The largest segment is now Navy and aerospace work, so defense budgets and program timing drive more of the cash flow that services debt | 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 85; calculations |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

ESCO signed a share purchase agreement on 2026-04-15 to buy Megger Group Limited, a testing and monitoring supplier to utilities, from TBG AG for about USD 2.35 billion, of which about USD 0.9 billion is cash and about USD 1.4 billion is ESCO equity. The cash is to come from existing cash and incremental debt with committed financing in place, Megger will join the Utility Solutions Group, regulatory filings are under way, and closing was expected in the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The annual report names Megger as a significant competitor of that segment.

On 2026-05-29 ESCO and certain subsidiaries signed a credit agreement with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as administrative agent and Bank of America, N.A. as syndication agent, to finance the purchase. It provides a USD 500 million senior secured revolving facility, a USD 500 million senior secured term loan A and a USD 500 million senior secured term loan B. The revolver and term loan A mature five years after the effective date and term loan B seven years after it. An expansion option allows more revolver or term loans up to the greater of USD 451 million or 100% of Consolidated EBITDA plus further amounts subject to leverage tests. The facility becomes effective on conditions that include the Megger closing, and it replaces the existing facility on that date.

The existing facility is a USD 500 million revolver and an incremental term loan, both maturing on 2028-08-30, secured by guaranties of material U.S. subsidiaries and a pledge of the equity of material foreign subsidiaries; USD 85 million was drawn at 2026-06-30. No bonds, notes or other debt securities are described in the seven documents. The credit agreements themselves are not supplied, so covenant levels, baskets and guarantor lists are not established. Nothing in the sources states Megger's revenue, earnings, debt or cash, the number or issue price of the ESCO shares, the terms of the Shareholder Agreement, or whether the deal has closed, so pro forma leverage and the size of TBG AG's holding are not established.

spans.text: # CP-2 Fundamental credit for ESCO TECHNOLOGIES INC (ese)
## Request

Fundamental credit for ESCO TECHNOLOGIES INC (ese), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the overall fundamental credit profile of ESCO, its strongest support and its primary downside path, built on the financial foundation and the business and governance analysis of the seven supplied documents.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

ESCO's standalone credit profile is strong, with net debt at 0.04x EBITDA on 2026-06-30, but the pending Megger acquisition would lift it to 2.98x pro forma, a step-up creditors cannot size because Megger's earnings, debt and the new facility's covenants are not supplied.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C04

Net debt was USD 11.76 million at 2026-06-30, USD 13.86 million after the dividend paid on 2026-07-17 and USD 13.84 million after the one scheduled for 2026-10-15, both 0.05x, and USD 911.76 million pro forma for the Megger cash price of USD 0.9 billion, with closing expected in the first quarter of fiscal 2027. Cash and the undrawn revolver of USD 515.54 million cover total debt of USD 85 million, or 6.07x.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C10; calculation C11
### Key findings

Standalone leverage and coverage leave a wide cushion before any acquisition debt. Total debt was USD 85 million, or 0.28x last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 305.68 million, against 0.76x at 2025-09-30, and EBITDA covered cash interest 20.42x against 14.09x in fiscal 2025. Debt fell because the VACCO proceeds were used primarily to pay down borrowings after the Maritime purchase, so the acquisition debt did not stay in place, and the ratios use reported EBITDA with Maritime counted only from 2025-04-25.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C05; calculation C41

Liquidity is ample against the debt, and no maturity of size falls before 2028-08-30. Cash of USD 73.24 million and the undrawn USD 442.3 million of the revolver give USD 515.54 million, 6.07x total debt and 25.78x the USD 20 million due within twelve months, with USD 45 million of revolver borrowings and USD 12.7 million of letters of credit already deducted. Liquidity is USD 50.71 million lower than at 2025-09-30, which reflects repaid term debt and the cash tax on the VACCO gain, not operating weakness; the revolver and term loan A both mature on 2028-08-30.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C07; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C39; calculation C40

Cash generation is good, but part of it is timing. Free cash flow was USD 258.10 million over the last twelve months, 84.44% of EBITDA against 60.41% in fiscal 2025 and 41.04% in fiscal 2024, helped by customer advances: contract liabilities rose 33.04% to USD 288.14 million since 2025-09-30. A full reversal of the USD 71.55 million increase would use 97.70% of cash but only 13.88% of liquidity, so the timing benefit is not a liquidity risk on its own, but part of the improvement in conversion will not repeat.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C06; calculation C16; calculation C15; calculation C14; calculation C21; calculation C09; calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C19

The Megger acquisition is the dominant credit event and cannot yet be sized. Net debt to EBITDA would rise from 0.04x to 2.98x pro forma for the cash price, with closing expected in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, and that figure uses ESCO's own EBITDA only, with no Megger earnings and no Megger debt. The total price of about USD 2.35 billion is 7.69x ESCO's last-twelve-months EBITDA and 97.11% of its total assets, the cash part alone is 2.94x, and the equity part, 59.57% of the price, adds no debt but adds a shareholder. As an illustration, interest on USD 0.9 billion at the existing facility's recent average rate of 5.18% would be about USD 46.62 million a year, 15.25% of last-twelve-months EBITDA, but the new facility's pricing is not supplied.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C22; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C26; calculation C27

Revenue is visible but concentrated in defense. Backlog of USD 1,540.5 million is 1.19x last-twelve-months net sales and about 59% of it is expected to convert within twelve months; entered orders were 1.43x net sales over nine months. ### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The view could be too cautious. The equity part of about USD 1.4 billion is 59.57% of the price and adds no debt, the financing is committed, total debt at 2026-06-30 was below its USD 122 million level before the Maritime purchase, and Megger's own earnings, which would lower the 2.98x figure, are not counted in it. It could also be too optimistic: reported EBITDA includes Maritime from 2025-04-25 and a customer-advance benefit, backlog conversion depends on government funding, and the covenant levels and new facility terms are unseen.

The view would improve if Megger's earnings and debt, once supplied, showed combined leverage at or below the pro forma figure, and if the covenant package left wide headroom. ### Strengths and weaknesses

The first credit strength is low standalone leverage with high coverage. Total debt of USD 85 million is 0.28x EBITDA and cash interest is covered 20.42x, so a large fall in earnings would still leave interest comfortably covered: halving last-twelve-months EBITDA would still give 10.21x cover. That keeps default probability low on the standalone business.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C28

The second is liquidity with no near maturity. Cash plus the undrawn revolver of USD 515.54 million is 6.07x total debt, and the facility matures on 2028-08-30, so there is no refinancing pressure on the existing structure before the Megger closing.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C10; calculation C11

The third is visible demand and rising margins. Backlog of USD 1,540.5 million is 1.19x annual sales, orders exceed sales, and EBITDA margin rose from 21.58% in fiscal 2024 to 23.68% over the last twelve months, which supports debt service through a cycle.

The fourth is a financial policy that has repaid debt and kept distributions small. Dividends took 4.12% of operating cash flow and the VACCO proceeds went primarily to debt, which lowers leakage and improves recovery prospects.

### Business, ownership and revenue drivers

ESCO makes engineered products and services for three businesses, aerospace and defense (filtration, fluid control and naval signature and power systems), utility testing and diagnostics, and RF test and measurement, and revenue visibility comes from backlog of USD 1,540.5 million, with no customer above 10% of sales. That supports debt service capacity because orders are placed ahead of delivery, but government customers at 31.63% of sales and over-time revenue at 45.18% tie cash flow to program funding and cost estimates.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 21

Ownership is public, with no sponsor or controlling holder named, a classified board and a two-thirds merger vote under Missouri law that entrench the incumbent board, and a pending Shareholder Agreement with the Megger seller that is not supplied. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk as medium, so the financial policy view rests on conduct to date, not on legal limits.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 30

Revenue drivers are volume and price: net sales rose 14.40% in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, of which 8% was organic, and price increases are cited in all three segments' margin commentary. Pricing power is partial: fixed-price contracts and government customers limit pass-through of cost inflation, and sole-source suppliers can cut volume. Recurring versus transactional revenue and contract duration are not disclosed, so revenue durability rests on backlog and segment data.
### Margins and cash conversion

Reported EBITDA margin has risen from 19.50% in fiscal 2023 to 23.68% over the last twelve months, helped by volume leverage and price increases against inflation and unfavorable mix. The split between fixed and variable cost is not disclosed, so operating leverage cannot be measured; the main protections are price increases, capital expenditure of only 3.32% of sales and restructuring in the USG and Test segments, and the main exposures are tariffs, raw material cost and cost estimates on fixed-price work.

### Competitive forces, external factors and opportunities and threats

Competitive rivalry is broad and global, with named competitors in each segment including Parker Hannifin, Moog and TransDigm in aerospace, Megger and OMICRON in utility testing and Rohde & Schwarz in shielding, and competition is driven by quality, technology, price and delivery, so no single factor protects margin. The company points to patented technology and Doble's reserve of empirical data as barriers to new entrants (Management Language), which would support margin durability if they hold. Substitution is not described as a risk for qualified aerospace and naval products, and the pressure at NRG comes from renewables policy rather than from substitutes. Buyer power is meaningful: government contracts can be terminated for the customer's convenience and appropriations can delay orders, though no customer exceeds 10% of sales. Supplier power is concentrated in sole-source parts, such as the single manufacturer behind about 23% of Doble products and Globe's single supplier of critical materials.

Macro and policy factors are material to credit here, so the external-factor review is kept. Political and regulatory: defense spending priorities, export controls and tariffs, UK naval funding and trade tension with China can delay orders or raise costs, and Asia is a tenth of sales. Economic: inflation squeezes fixed-price margins, and interest rates apply to the floating-rate bank debt. Technological and end-market: broad-based utility demand and data-center filters lifted Doble and Test orders, while the expiry of U.S. renewables tax credits cut NRG orders.

Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the Doble order momentum, data-center demand for Test filters, an equity-funded Megger that adds earnings without full debt funding, and further backlog conversion. Threats that could weaken it are a funding delay on Navy programs, a leveraged Megger integration, tariff and supply shocks, renewables weakness at NRG and cyber or compliance incidents in a decentralized organization. The strengths and weaknesses are in the section above.
### Outlook

Over the next 12 to 24 months the near-term signals are favorable and the main uncertainty is the closing. Management guides fiscal 2026 sales to USD 1.30 billion to USD 1.33 billion, which implies fourth-quarter sales of USD 361.97 million to USD 391.97 million, growth of 2.64% to 11.14% on the same quarter of fiscal 2025 against 14.40% in the third quarter, so guidance implies slower growth even though backlog is 1.19x last-twelve-months sales. The Megger closing is expected between October and December 2026, so at the 2026-11-05 cutoff the facility swap and the new shareholder may already have occurred.

### Downside scenario

A realistic downside starts with a delay or cut in U.S. Government funding for Navy submarine programs, which Globe and Westland depend on and which the company says can extend beyond a single year, arriving while Megger has closed and the new term loans are drawn. The first operational break is in A&D, the largest segment at 49.29% of nine-month sales: program deliveries slip, backlog converts later, and customer advances stop growing, so the USD 71.55 million build in contract liabilities starts to reverse. EBITDA and operating cash flow fall together, free cash flow conversion drops back toward the 60.41% of fiscal 2025, and on today's liquidity of USD 515.54 million, 7.21x the contract liability build, the reversal alone would be absorbed, although liquidity after closing depends on the new revolver and the cash used for the price, which are not established.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_ese-20250930x10k.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ese-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C17; calculation C10; calculation C20; calculation C15

The financial consequence depends on the Megger debt. On ESCO's own EBITDA, net debt to EBITDA would already stand at 2.98x after the cash price, and any EBITDA fall raises it mechanically, but the size of the fall that would breach a covenant cannot be computed because covenant levels, the new facility's pricing and Megger's earnings are not supplied. Standalone, interest cover would stay at 10.21x even if EBITDA halved, and management levers are the dividend of USD 8.26 million, the unused buyback authority, capital expenditure of only 3.32% of sales and the equity portion of the Megger price. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress on the standalone business; after closing it cannot be confirmed, and the observable triggers are the closing notice, the drawn amounts under the new term loans, the first covenant disclosure and the next quarter's backlog and orders.

### Overall credit view

Overall, ESCO presents a strong standalone business profile supported by net debt of USD 11.76 million, cash interest cover of 20.42x, liquidity of USD 515.54 million and backlog of USD 1,540.5 million, but credit quality is constrained by the pending Megger acquisition, which would lift net debt to USD 911.76 million pro forma and add a shareholder whose rights are unknown. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because conversion is 84.44% of EBITDA over the last twelve months against 60.41% in fiscal 2025, part of the gap is customer-advance timing, and part of the demand rests on government funding. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the Megger closing and the terms of the new facility, since the existing facility matures on 2028-08-30 and no rating or market data are supplied. The primary downside path is a government funding delay at A&D arriving after Megger closes with debt-funded cash. Further analysis would require Megger's financial statements, the credit agreements and the Shareholder Agreement. The module is ready with limitations, because the source gate is partly met: the seven public documents and the three earlier analyses are present, but the credit agreements and Megger's financials are not. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: the leverage step-up from the Megger acquisition.
